Showed trace waterfall, request inspector, KV cache indicators, and rollout/fallback policies. Agreed next steps: share logs, run targeted replay/benchmark, and provide security docs & pricing.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-21 11:00 PT / 19:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Romero (Redwood AE), Priya Kothari (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (PolarisTech), Sarah Chen (PolarisTech CTO), Ibrahim Nadeem (Platform)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, this is Priya on the engineering side. Quick intro?
[00:08] Marcus: Yep, Marcus here, lead ML engineer at PolarisTech - we run a mix of batch and low-latency real time features behind a service mesh in AWS.
[00:14] Sarah: Sarah here, CTO. We're evaluating observability for model inference and want to see how Redwood helps track down errors and latency regressions.
[00:20] Priya: Great. Our plan — walkthrough the Console request inspector, traces, playback, and then dig into KV cache indicators and rollout/fallback flows. We'll also highlight how you'd run a dedicated pool vs hosted API.
[00:33] Ibrahim: Quick note — we have strict residency and KMS rules, so private deployment might be required.
[00:38] Alex: Noted. We'll surface that in the security docs. Okay jumping into the Console. Sorry transcript: small audio glitch.
[01:05] Priya: (screen) Here is the Requests view. You can filter by model, route, tenant, and the request id. For each request we show a trace waterfall. Let me click one that had an error — you can see time spent in queuing, model exec, and post-processing.
[01:30] Marcus: That waterfall is handy. Does queuing include the batching window?
[01:36] Priya: Yes, queuing reflects time waiting in the batcher. It shows batch size and whether prefix cache hit occurred. Notice this one shows a "kay-vee cache" — KV cache showed a miss so it rehydrated. (laughs) The transcription picked that wrong.
[01:52] Ibrahim: When it rehydrated, we saw a 300ms spike. Can we replay that exact request to reproduce?
[01:58] Priya: Absolutely. The request inspector has a playback control. You can replay at real-time or accelerated pace. We also replay behind the same routing policy — so if you want to test dedicated vs hosted variants we can route to the dedicated pool.
[02:20] Sarah: What's the fidelity of playback? Will it run against the same model weights and quantization?
[02:27] Priya: Good question. For hosted we replay against the pinned model version you selected. For private/Dedicated we replay against whatever binary is deployed in that pool. Quantization and kernel selection are preserved if you've pinned the model variant.
[02:42] Marcus: We have edge-case failures where the model returns an empty answer intermittently. Could that be a KV cache or tokenization mismatch?
[02:51] Priya: Possibly. In the trace you can expand the tokenization stage and see input length, token mapping diffs, and any pre/post hooks. Often the problem is pre-processing or a prompt rollout.
[03:05] Alex: Maybe run a paired example — show the same request replayed with a canary rollout and then rollback after seeing divergence.
[03:12] Priya: Sure. (screen) Here's a rollout panel: you can do canary at 5%, A/B, or immediate. When a canary hits error thresholds we can auto-fallback to the previous model — you'll see that in the traces as a rerouted request.
[03:31] Ibrahim: How do we configure error thresholds? Per-route? Per-tenant?
[03:37] Priya: Both. SLOs are per-route by default but you can override at tenant level. Thresholds are based on latency percentiles, error rates, and custom checks like token-length mismatches.
[03:46] Marcus: Any way to see aggregated error trends tied to prompt sets? We run multiple prompt templates for different customers.
[03:52] Priya: Yes, Optimize ties prompts to eval sets. In Console you can tag requests with prompt-template metadata and run regressions across versions. We'll show a quick screenshot of that integration.
[04:12] Alex: Quick pause — do you have compliance questions? I can jump in.
[04:18] Sarah: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, and SSO are the immediate ones. Also we want to know about data retention for request logs.
[04:25] Alex: We support SSO via SAML/OIDC, audit logs with export, and KMS integration for private deployments. For hosted API we have configurable retention windows and can do longer retention for enterprise add-on. We'll add our security whitepaper to the follow-up.
[04:40] Ibrahim: If we go private, do we still have the Console SaaS control plane?
[04:44] Priya: In Private mode the control plane can be customer-managed in your VPC. There's an option for fully air-gapped on-prem install if needed.
[04:52] Marcus: Back to replay — when you replay, do we get identical latency characteristics? We're trying to surface stochastic model variance vs infra.
[04:59] Priya: Replays reproduce the request path but you will see variance if the model is non-deterministic. For infra signals like batching and queuing, replay with pinned kernels will be consistent. We also record host metrics at time of request so you can compare.
[05:18] Marcus: Can we tag requests with correlation IDs from our service mesh?
[05:22] Priya: Yes, you can push your correlation id metadata; it surfaces in the request inspector and trace filters.
[05:28] Ibrahim: We have a custom in-house router for traffic shaping. Can Redwood run a traffic mirror for a percentage of live traffic?
[05:35] Priya: We support traffic mirroring and can apply it to canary traffic. This is how many of our customers do realtime smoke tests in prod without impacting live users.
[05:44] Sarah: Pricing question — how do you charge for replayed requests in a PoC?
[05:48] Alex: We'll include a PoC package; replays count as inference calls for billing but PoC credits can be allocated. We'll give a tailored price sheet.
[05:56] Marcus: There's an error we hit where the request is rerouted to fallback model but still shows as success in the upstream. Can you show the logs that map the reroute?
[06:04] Priya: Yeah, in the trace expand the routing metadata — you'll see an event for "fallback: true" and a pair of request ids. The request inspector links both requests and you can compare token deltas and outputs.
[06:19] Ibrahim: Sometimes the console index search is slow; is that a known latency issue?
[06:23] Priya: We've got pagination and index sharding; if you store a lot of logs and long retention it can slow down search. We recommend exporting large datasets to the customer S3 bucket.
[06:34] Marcus: For the replay, can we replay against a locally-built quantized binary?
[06:39] Priya: If you're on Dedicated or Private you can deploy your quantized binary and we can route replay to it. For hosted we only allow approved model binaries.
[06:48] Alex: Showcasing the request timeline — see how we mark KV cache hits. We'll intentionally replay a cached and a non-cached request.
[06:59] Priya: (screen) This request has a "cache_hit": true and shows 40ms served from cache. This other one shows cache_miss and 420ms rehydrate. You can add a prewarming policy to reduce cold rehydrates.
[07:17] Marcus: Prewarming sounds good. How do you measure cost impact?
[07:21] Alex: Console has token-level cost breakdown and per-request cost estimate. Optimize can recommend quantization or batching parameters to reduce unit cost.
[07:30] Ibrahim: Is KV cache implemented in memory on GPU instance or external store?
[07:34] Priya: It's an in-memory cache co-located with the model process for low-latency K-V retrieval. For large KVs we stream from a backing store but that incurs network latency.
[07:44] Sarah: If KMS keys are customer-managed, do logs include plaintext?
[07:48] Alex: No, we never store raw secrets; request payloads can be masked and you can configure PII scrubbing for logs. For private deployments you control key material.
[07:58] Marcus: Demo: can you reproduce a failing request now? I'll paste an example request id.
[08:02] Marcus: (paste) request-20260821-77ab9
[08:07] Priya: Pulling it up... there are two related requests — one routed to canary, one to fallback. The canary shows an empty result. Let me replay the canary at 1x speed.
[08:25] (audio: clicking, slight pause)
[08:35] Priya: Replay done. The trace shows tokenization produced an unusual token boundary and a post-hook returned an empty generation. There's also a model exec log showing `null` generation at 0.0 probability - looks like an early stop.
[08:52] Marcus: That aligns with logs we saw. Could that be a prompt template change?
[08:56] Priya: Very possible — look at the preprocessor diff tab. Yes, the prompt included an extra non-printable char. We surface those diffs in the inspector.
[09:10] Ibrahim: For our incident process, can we export the full trace and attach to JIRA?
[09:15] Priya: Yes export JSON or link. Export includes trace, logs, and host metrics.
[09:20] Alex: Recap for Marcus: we'll run a focused replay for 1k requests with sample traffic to measure latency/cost, and Priya will instrument a KV-cache stress test.
[09:32] Marcus: Sounds good. One more thing — do you offer sampling knobs so we don't store all request logs?
[09:38] Priya: You can sample at ingestion, or set conditional retention (keep only requests that hit error thresholds).
[09:44] Sarah: Are there RBAC controls for console access? We don't want devs to see customer PII.
[09:50] Alex: Yes, RBAC + field-level masking. We'll include a guide in the security doc.
[10:03] (short break in recording; meeting continues)
[10:50] Priya: Now showing the error-analysis panel. It groups by error class and shows sample stack traces and model outputs. You can expand a group to see percent of requests and a timeline of spikes.
[11:12] Marcus: Can we bind alerts to regressions against a baseline prompt set?
[11:16] Priya: Yes, you can tie alerts to eval regression thresholds in Optimize. The alert can trigger webhook, Slack, or create an incident in Opsgenie.
[11:30] Ibrahim: For the PoC, if we want to measure cold-start vs warmed model latency, any recommended config?
[11:36] Priya: Configure prewarmed slots in Dedicated capacity and use synthetic replay to simulate concurrency. We'll include a suggested benchmark script.
[11:48] Marcus: Any gotchas for using our own quantized builds? We saw weird output differences in-house.
[11:54] Priya: Quantization differences can change token logits; we recommend baseline QA on a small eval set and run Optimize's regression checks. Also ensure compilation kernel matches sequence length distribution.
[12:08] Sarah: Timeline question — if we want a production pilot, how long to onboard?
[12:12] Alex: For Hosted a few days to a week. For Dedicated typical is 2-4 weeks including capacity planning. Private can be 4+ weeks depending on network approvals. We'll propose a timeline in the follow-up.
[12:25] Marcus: Any reference customers in fintech/healthcare with private deployments?
[12:28] Alex: Yes, will include a short list and anonymized case notes.
[12:33] Sarah: Okay good. Let's talk about specific SLOs — we need p99 latency under 500ms for user-facing feature.
[12:40] Priya: That is achievable with proper batching and prewarm. Optimize can recommend batching window ~20ms with micro-batching to keep tail low. We'll run a benchmark to validate.
[12:53] Ibrahim: One more technical question — does the trace ingest include GPU metrics, like kernel occupancy?
[12:58] Priya: We capture host level GPU metrics and correlate them to request windows. Kernel-level occupancy varies by runtime but we show memory and compute utilization.
[13:10] Marcus: Great. Any limitations on request size for replay?
[13:14] Priya: We support typical model sizes; extremely long histories may be truncated unless you configure extended sequences. We'll note the default token limits.
[13:25] Alex: Okay wrapping up — next steps and owners as Alex laid out. We'll also send a short build/PoC proposal.
[13:34] Sarah: Thanks, that was useful.
[13:36] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and the PoC slot.

End of meeting.
notes: Recording had two short drops; transcription picked up some product names wrong (e.g., "kay-vee cache"). Customer interested in private deployment and PoC focused on replay/benchmarks.
duration_alignment_note: Transcript timestamps are relative and cover key demo segments; total transcript trimmed to highlights but aligns with stated 52 minute duration.
